tagline: A ranch-country loop out of Lake George and back.
intro: The loop begins and ends in the village of Lake George. One leg follows NY 9N southwest 11 miles to Lake Luzerne, where the Sacandaga comes down a gorge into the Hudson. The other runs up to Warrensburg on the Schroon River and out through the town of Stony Creek. Horse ranches and lakeside resort villages fill the 40 miles in between.

Thomas Jefferson called Lake George the Queen of the American Lakes. Long before the resorts, armies of the colonial wars passed this way between the British and French colonies, and later the steamboats ran from the railroad docks up the lake to the hotels.

moments.title: Hadley
moments.text: Just above where the Sacandaga meets the Hudson, the Hadley Bow Bridge crosses the gorge on iron chords that arch both above and below its deck, the last of its kind in the state.

moments.title: Stony Creek
moments.text: While a tannery worked where Roaring Branch meets Stony Creek, the town reached 1,250 people, and once the hemlocks were cut out and tanning changed, the tannery closed and the town shrank.

moments.title: Lake George
moments.text: The village at the foot of the lake, first called Caldwell, keeps a reconstruction of Fort William Henry and kept one mayor for more than half a century.

sources.label: Adirondack Regional Tourism Council, Adirondack North Country Scenic Byways (p. 8)
